title: Third-party weights flagging and human review queue for model ingestion
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a reliable, auditable flow to detect third-party/encumbered model weights during ingestion, automatically flag borderline cases, place artifacts into a quarantine state, and surface a prioritized human review queue for legal/compliance to approve, reject, or request remediation. This ticket defines the product acceptance criteria, the review UX in Console, required metadata enrichment for provenance, and the fallback behaviors for serving and publishing performance profiles.

Background/context:
- Current onboarding pipeline accepts model uploads with a basic license field and free-text notes; there is no structured flagging for partial-encumbrances (e.g., models trained on proprietary datasets, mixed-weights, or redistributed checkpoints with unclear licenses).
- Past incidents demonstrated risk: a model shipped to hosted customers without proper license provenance, triggering legal review and temporary model delisting.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
1) Introduce deterministic detection heuristics (hash-based weight signatures, file name heuristics, and user-supplied provenance metadata) that mark an upload as one of: clean, suspicious, encumbered, or explicitly restricted.
2) Quarantine flow: quarantined model artifacts cannot be published to the catalog, cannot be used in hosted tenant default routes, and are discoverable only in a review workspace.
3) Human review queue: Console view for legal/compliance with filters (severity, model size, submitter, detected issues), action buttons (approve, request-more-info, reject, escalate), and audit trail entries exported to S3.
4) Version pinning policy: if a new model version is quarantined, previous pinned versions remain active unless explicitly delisted.
5) Performance profile publishing: only models marked as approved may have their performance profiles (latency/cost/quality benchmarks) published to the public catalog; quarantined or suspicious models get internal-only profiles if allowed.
6) Integrations: webhook to legal ticketing system (e.g., Zendesk/Jira), KMS for holding encrypted artifacts during quarantine, and an optional escrow flag for models requiring third-party escrow.

Acceptance criteria:
- Detection pipeline implemented with unit tests and a dataset of known encumbered examples (test coverage >= 85%).
- Console review UI mockups approved by Legal and PM (link to design spec).
- Quarantine state enforced in ingestion service: quarantined uploads cannot be published or consumed by default hosted routes.
- Audit log entries include uploader, detection reasons, hash signatures, timestamp, reviewer decisions, and links to evidence.
- Exportable CSV/JSON of the review queue and an API endpoint for programmatic approval/rejection.
- Rollout plan documented; default behavior on rollout: non-blocking for existing production models, quarantine enforced for all new uploads.

Design & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONB/Third-Party+Weights+Flagging (design spec, triage decision matrix, and detection heuristics).
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/Example/Model-Review-Console (mockups for reviewer queue and model detail panel).
- Compliance checklist: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/model-onboarding-compliance

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Heuristics vs. ML classifier: initial phase will be deterministic heuristics for auditability; consider ML classifier in Phase 2 if false positive rate remains high.
- Owner for escrow operations: Legal + Ops will need a runbook for escrow triggers (time-bound holds vs. permanent quarantine).
- Serving fallback: should frozen/pinned fallback be automatically selected for tenant routes when the latest version is quarantined? PM preference: yes, but requires ENG support for automatic routing.

Implementation notes for Eng: (for engineering reference)
- Ingestion pipeline change points: pre-processing step that calculates weight file hashes, extracts wheel/tar manifests, and checks signatures against internal encumbered DB.
- New artifact metadata fields: provenance_source, provenance_url, original_checksum, encumbrance_score, quarantine_reason, reviewer_decision, review_ticket_id. (These will be stored as top-level strings in model metadata.)
- API: POST /ingest returns status {accepted|quarantined|rejected} and a review_url when quarantined.
- Backwards compatibility: existing model upload clients must continue to work; add a warning header for uploads that trigger suspicion heuristics.

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (beta): internal + partners only; quarantine enforced but auto-notifications to uploader explain remediation steps.
Phase 2: public rollout with stricter heuristics and webhook to legal ticketing.

Risks & mitigation:
- False positives block valid open models: include explicit override paths and expedited review SLA (24h default for high-priority partners).
- Operational overhead for Legal: provide bulk triage tools and batching for similar detections.

Notes on related tickets and history:
- Related: PM-6310 (model-source-validation and artifact approval) — reuse parts of that matrix.
- Dependent on ENG-2211 (ingest metadata schema and audit log), and ENG-2267 (console review widgets).

Next steps / Action items:
- PM: finalize acceptance criteria and coordinate Legal + Security sign-off (owner: Aisha).
- Design: produce high-fidelity Console screens for queue and model detail (owner: Priya Shah).
- Eng: prototype deterministic heuristics and quarantine enforcement on staging (owner: Diego).
- Legal: draft reviewer decision taxonomy and support runbook (owner: Marco Liu).
